profile.name: Uzbekistani dance
profile.tagline: Ice dance representation from Uzbekistan in international competition
profile.insight: In 2012, Uzbekistani ice dancer Viktor Kovalenko received his visa on 26 March, arrived in Nice 30 minutes before competing, and reached the arena 10 minutes prior to qualifying.
profile.profile: Uzbekistani ice dance in international sports competition is represented by skaters competing under the flag of Uzbekistan, such as Viktor Kovalenko. Partners representing the nation have included Anna Nagornyuk, Elizaveta Tretiakova, Maria Popkova, and Viola Zakhliupana. Competitions entered include the ISU Junior Grand Prix, World Junior Championships, Four Continents Championships, and World Championships. Performance disciplines follow ice dance standards set by international skating bodies.
profile.profile_long:
Uzbekistani dance in the context of international figure skating and ice dance includes athletes representing Uzbekistan in global events regulated by the International Skating Union. Competitors such as Viktor Vyacheslavovich Kovalenko, born on 6 December 1991, have performed on both junior and senior international levels across multiple seasons. Kovalenko's early career involved competing alongside partner Maria Popkova, with whom he placed 24th at the 2010 World Junior Championships.

In the 2011–2012 season, Kovalenko began competing with Anna Nagornyuk. The pair competed on the 2011–12 ISU Junior Grand Prix series before making their senior international debut at the 2012 Four Continents Championships, where they finished in 8th place. They went on to finish 12th at the 2012 World Junior Championships and qualified to compete at the senior 2012 World Championships in Nice, France. Their participation in Nice involved precise timing due to travel delays: while Nagornyuk received her visa a week prior, Kovalenko was granted his visa on the morning of 26 March, the day of the preliminary round. He arrived in Nice half an hour before scheduled competition and reached the arena ten minutes before competing, successfully qualifying for the short dance.

During the 2012–2013 season, Nagornyuk and Kovalenko secured 10th place finishes at both the Four Continents Championships and the World Junior Championships before parting ways. Prior to the 2013–2014 season, Kovalenko partnered with Elizaveta Tretiakova. Their planned appearance at the 2013 Nebelhorn Trophy—an Olympic qualifying event for the 2014 Winter Olympics—was interrupted when Kovalenko contracted chicken pox just before the event. International databases also record partnerships involving Viola Zakhliupana.
